title: OpenAI Achieves Milestone in Automated Research Internship, Internal Agent Runs 3.1 Times Longer Than Human

content_html:
Recently, the field of artificial intelligence has once again witnessed a milestone breakthrough. OpenAI officially announced that its internal system has successfully achieved the important milestone of "automated research intern." This means that under the supervision and guidance of humans, the system is now capable of independently completing well-defined complex tasks that typically take senior researchers several days to accomplish.

According to internal operational data, the penetration rate of artificial intelligence has exceeded traditional expectations. As of mid-August this year, the ratio of agents to humans within OpenAI's core research organization has reached 3.1 to 1. Specifically, if calculated based on a standard 8-hour workday, for every human workday invested, the research organization consumes as much as 3.1 agent workdays of runtime.

It should be clarified that this remarkable 3.1:1 ratio measures the actual runtime and workload of agents, and does not directly equate to equivalent productivity output. Nevertheless, it clearly reflects that the parallel working model of agents has been deeply embedded and reshaped the daily research ecosystem within OpenAI.

Regarding this industry trend, OpenAI employee Kevin Liu expressed a profound view. He pointed out that recursive self-improvement is likely to become the most crucial factor driving the exponential leap in AI capabilities in the coming years. However, such cutting-edge technological advancements often remain confined within a few top AI laboratories by default. Therefore, industry transparency is more urgent than ever. Only in this way can the public have the necessary basis for discussion, jointly explore whether and how to scientifically control the pace of future model development. At the same time, he also publicly called on other AI companies around the world to adopt the same transparent and open attitude.
